expectations.text: Explicitly explains why violin is better than box plot for bimodal data
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'Unlike box plots, violin plots show the full density profile of each endpoint's response times. This is critical because you explicitly have bimodal distributions -- a box plot would hide the two peaks entirely, collapsing them into a single median and interquartile range.'

expectations.text: Mentions that box plots hide bimodality
expectations.evidence: Stated twice: (1) 'a box plot would hide the two peaks entirely' in the violin plot section, and (2) 'Hides bimodality entirely. Two very different distributions can produce identical box plots.' in the 'What to Avoid' table.

expectations.text: Considers the sample size (10K per endpoint) in the recommendation
expectations.evidence: Dedicated subsection 'Handles 10,000 points well' explains that violin plots use KDE to summarize large datasets. Also references '10,000 points per endpoint (30,000 total)' when discussing why raw scatter/strip plots fall short.

expectations.text: Provides a plotly code example for the violin plot
expectations.evidence: Implementation Notes section includes: 'Python (Plotly): px.violin(df, x="endpoint", y="response_time", box=True, points=False) for an interactive version.' This is a working Plotly Express one-liner, though it is not a full multi-line code block with imports.

claims.claim: Violin plots use kernel density estimation to summarize large datasets smoothly
claims.evidence: This is a well-known property of violin plots -- they are built on KDE by definition.

claims.claim: Two very different distributions can produce identical box plots
claims.evidence: This is a well-documented limitation of box plots. Distributions with different shapes but similar quartiles will produce identical box plots.

claims.claim: The mean of a bimodal distribution may sit in a valley between the two modes
claims.evidence: Correct by definition -- for bimodal distributions the mean often falls between modes where density is low.

claims.claim: Seaborn's cut=0 prevents the KDE from extending beyond observed data
claims.evidence: This is correct per Seaborn documentation for sns.violinplot.
Correct per Plotly Express documentation -- box=True overlays a box plot inside the violin.
